newsitem.title: CANADA: Arbor gets lift from Loewen bid.
newsitem.headline: Arbor gets lift from Loewen bid.

text.p: Shares in Arbor Memorial Services Inc jumped on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday as the Canadian funeral home operator received a boost from a takeover bid for Loewen Group Inc.
Arbor Memorial's class A stock rose 1.50 to 25 in light midday trading, leading net gainers on the TSE.
Analysts said the the market is re-evaluating Arbor Memorial in the wake of Service Corp International's US$4.1 billion bid for Vancouver-based Loewen on Tuesday.
Houston-based Service is offering US$43 a share for Loewen and has said it may sweeten its bid.
"People are using the same valuation that Service Corp put on Loewen and applying it to Arbor," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd.

Shares in Loewen, North America's second biggest funeral home operator, slipped 1.40 to 53.55 on 321,000 shares. The stock soared to a new high of 57 on the initial news of the takeover offer on Tuesday.
Analysts said they expect Loewen to fight the surprise bid from its rival Service Corp, the continent's number one funeral home company.
